entry: One commit, one session, no code. A grilling session run under a standing order that no question reaches the operator: every frontier question was routed to a qualified source instead. Seven research subagents ran — vendor documentation, practitioner ground truth, a live API probe, published user pain, static-analysis prior art, competitive landscape, and a solo-segment sweep — and all seven wrote cited reports to docs/research/ rather than into the working window. The operator supplied one input the agents could not reach, a Reddit-derived causal synthesis, which closed the session's largest acknowledged blind spot and produced its sharpest mechanism: the config file asks users to declare the schema whose instability is their actual complaint. Three earlier conclusions were reversed by evidence and each reversal was written into an artifact rather than left in conversation, on the reasoning that chat is discarded at /clear and a kill criterion that would have stopped the project on a settled fact is not. The session's own worst moment is recorded in memory: the first round posed six questions to the operator, at least two of which were answered in a PRD the repo cited and the agent had not read.

Two streams and one operator correction that reframed both. The demand-test instruments were built and then rebuilt: the first draft ghostwrote five outreach messages in the operator's first person, which he rejected outright, and the fix was to produce content specifications instead so the words stay his. LinkedIn was excluded entirely and SewerAI ruled off any contact list, which closed cold outreach and left three channels. The session's sharpest finding came from the operator, not the agent: he had already converted this exact buyer once, through a free structural diagnosis posted publicly on Reddit, and the engagement that followed was never signed and never paid because the buyer had engineers and now had a portable answer. PRODUCT.md had predicted that outcome in writing before it happened. The recruiting artifact written that same morning had concluded the buyer has no public channel, on the strength of two research agents being unable to load Reddit; a tooling limitation had been written down as a fact about the market, and the correction is now in the file. The prior-art sweep then ran nine passes and adversarially verified sixteen keystone claims, correcting nine and catching one misattribution, one falsified standing claim in PRODUCT.md, and one source that fabricated enum values the verifier then refused to trust for anything else. The audit scout falsified its own brief. The best model for the coverage manifest turned out to be CONSORT and PRISMA rather than financial audit, and was found only because a scout flagged its own unpursued lead and was sent back for it. Worst moment: the state directory was gitignored as scratch, so the session record this entry belongs to would have survived only on one disk, and the agent noticed and moved on rather than fixing it until told to.

One decision, spent from a sweep banked the session before. The session-start claim check earned its place immediately: the handoff said the refuted SARIF sentence stood in PRODUCT.md, and it stood in three files; it said to delete plan-tier rate-limit figures, and those figures were in no canonical doc at all. Both corrections landed before any writing began. The ADR itself was authored twice — the first pass ran at default reasoning effort and the operator interrupted it to relaunch at high, which changed the output from a transcription of the research findings into a model reasoned over them. Five things came out of the second pass that the handoff had not specified: evidence sufficiency took three values rather than two, on the test that a value earns its place only if it changes the operator's next action; conformity became absent rather than gaining a third value, because a verdict never formed is not a verdict; ISA 705's adverse opinion was dropped because it turns on a materiality judgement a CLI cannot compute; pervasiveness was defined structurally rather than as a percentage, since any threshold would be computed over a denominator the scan has just admitted it cannot establish; and the funnel gained a fifth stage, enumeration, because that is the only place unbounded gaps arise and the disclaimed disposition keys on them. The sharpest correction was to the handoff's own instruction. It said to adopt XCCDF's rule that a non-verdict never enters a scoring denominator. Applied alone that rule IS the Great Expectations defect — excluding never-run checks from the denominator is exactly how a half-unrun suite reports 100 percent. The rule as written is stronger: the conformity ratio and the coverage ratio are published together or not at all. Worst moment: the first pass was already several paragraphs in before the operator stopped it, which means the effort setting was never considered against the artifact's blast radius until someone else did it.

The session that was supposed to write one ADR ran the proof instead, and the proof spent three of the repository's standing beliefs. ADR-0005 landed first and cleanly: the outcome enum split into conformity and evidence sufficiency, with five judgment calls the handoff had not specified and one correction to the handoff's own instruction, because XCCDF's exclude-from-scoring rule applied alone IS the Great Expectations defect it was meant to prevent. Then the setup went badly in a way worth keeping. A wizard was written to walk the operator through building a Notion fixture; the agent told him to run it through the harness, where stdin is not a terminal, so every prompt read EOF and the script recorded ten empty values plus a phantom REVOCATION_SUPPORTED=no — an invented answer to the most consequential question in the fixture, which the checkpoint had already declared would narrow a merged ADR. It was caught by inspecting .env rather than by any guard, and the guard was written afterwards. The second attempt failed on a hidden-input prompt that captured Ctrl-V as a literal control character and corrupted the token inside 161 bytes of paste escapes, producing an empty-bodied HTTP 400 that read like a server fault for three probes before the bytes were examined. The fix was to stop hiding the input and to verify the token against the API before writing it. The operator then asked whether building the fixture with a different identity would confound the measurement — a better question than any the agent had asked itself — and the answer, with two named caveats, went into the repo rather than the chat. The fixture was then built in five MCP calls after two failed wizard runs, which is the session's clearest lesson about instrument choice. The proof itself returned three findings in under ten minutes: ADR-0002 decision 4 hard-errors every healthy scan because request_status is conditional and absent from normal responses; ADR-0005's enumeration Revisit-if did not fire; and the detectable hole that notion-api-practice.md called the highest-value item to verify, because a completeness proof would rest on it, does not exist — a revoked child vanishes from its parent's child list entirely. Worst moment: hours before that, the agent read the operator's screenshot of a disconnect dialog and wrote into three surfaces that permissions could produce an unreached gap, labelling the same paragraph 'UI capability CONFIRMED; API consequence OPEN'. The label was correct and the inference beside it was not, and the API refuted it the same day.

A session that produced no product artifact and was probably worth more than one that did. It started with the operator asking whether anything remained undone, the agent checking git plumbing, finding a clean tree, and answering no. That answer was wrong: the project's SOP names GitHub issues as the tracker, and six gate events recording decision changes had reached it nowhere. He then asked for the GitHub work and there was a pile of it. When he pointed out that this was exactly why he had asked, the agent ran the sweep it should have run first — and the sweep was more valuable than the answer, because it found that six of the ten untriaged issues were not open questions at all but undocumented decisions, each already answered in store.json in wording matching the issue's own stated Default. The tracker and the state file had been disagreeing about what was settled for a day. Two claims the agent made during that sweep were wrong and were corrected by checking rather than by argument: the skill-rules file was where it belonged, not missing, and the existing PreToolUse guard had in fact fired on ADR-0005 and passed it. The genuine gap was narrower and more interesting — tracker writes go through Bash heredocs, so neither the prompt-keyed nudge nor the tool-surface-keyed file guard could see three issues that instruct a downstream reader on architectural decisions. A new guard closed it, and then blocked the commit that installed it, because its command regex was unanchored and matched prose inside a heredoc quoting the very anti-pattern it forbids. Worst moment, and it is the same one as the first: the agent reported a status by checking the pipes rather than the process, and only ran the real check after being told twice.

scope: ADR-0006 + the PRODUCT.md correction it depends on
entry: The session took issue #13 as a mechanism swap and found a larger limit inside it. #13 asked for one thing: ADR-0002 decision 4 makes the absence of request_status a hard error, the field is absent from every healthy response, so replace the presence check with the positive test the Notion reference prescribes. That part was mechanical. What was not mechanical was checking WHERE the field is documented, which nobody had done. It is documented on the data-source query reference and on neither /reference/intro#pagination -- the normative shared-envelope description -- nor /reference/get-block-children. Block children is the traversal spine of the scan: every page walk, every nested descent, every child_page discovery. It carries no truncation signal at all, so a complete enumeration and a silently truncated one return the same has_more: false, which is exactly the value that lied at the data-source cap before 2026-04-20. That was true before the ADR and it was written down nowhere. The second question #13 asked -- where does 'uninformative' sit on ADR-0005's evidence-sufficiency axis -- was answered against adding a fourth value, on ADR-0005's own governing rule: the absent case has no remedy, fires on 100% of runs, and a permanent universal qualifier is the mechanism ADR-0005's fourth Revisit-if predicts will train readers to skip the limitations half. The residual doubt moved into the sampling-risk statement, which now names the endpoints a run trusted blind and so carries per-run content instead of boilerplate. The Bannister sweep ran before the one invented part was written rather than after, and it found the part was not invented: Elasticsearch reports a capped hit count as hits.total.relation 'gte' rather than as a fact, OSIsoft PI Web API documents the identical silent-truncation failure, and fetch n+1 is the standard defence. The same refuted inference was then found standing in three places, which is the second time this repository has produced that pattern -- results.md section 1 mapped the absent case to unreached, store.json's corrections_pending copied that sentence forward, and PRODUCT.md's proof-test list still asserted that partial-scan detectability rested on child_page survival. All three corrected by reference or in place; the evidence record was not edited. The guard fired once, on the PR body, and was right: the body carried reviewer prompts but no Revisit-if. Worst moment: the PR was opened before the body had been checked against the discipline the repository installed a hook for one session earlier.

commit: 6968110 (trim merge); PR #22 merged as 3fe815f (745449d, f3dcd43); issues #18-#21 filed
entry: The session that audited yesterday's work and found it wrong. It opened on housekeeping the operator had not asked to keep: a survey of ~/.claude turned up 8 modified and 40 untracked files, and the S295 triage in skills_research had already classified seven of them without any of it ever being committed, so a published 57-skill verdict table was resting on artifacts that existed on one disk and in no commit. That was handed to a peer session verbatim rather than acted on, and the operator's ruling came back simple: do not touch any of it, it is probably superseded. The checkpoint trim that followed produced the session's first real catch. Each band ended with a pointer at the band before it, so archiving older bands broke every reference above the cut while losing ZERO normative claims, and the superset check went green over a file that could no longer reach its own constraints. Hoisting fixed it, and hoisting from the OLDEST source recovered two constraints the newest band had already silently shed. The archive exposed loss that was there before it. That went into context-hygiene as a step, and the recognizer immediately fired on the file being edited, because adding the step renumbered a list and left one reference pointing at the wrong step. Then the work the operator actually wanted. #16 transcribed six settled defaults into CONTEXT.md and found the interaction its own Revisit-if had asked about: fail-new-only governs the FINDINGS contribution to exit status alone, because ADR-0005 decision 4 made disposition and coverage independent inputs. It also found the same refuted stop-condition wording standing in CONTEXT.md after PRODUCT.md had been corrected, which is the third instance of that pattern in this repository. #15 was the one that mattered. Auditing the (C) tier first, on the reasoning that the tier which produced one falsehood is where the next one lives, the pass refuted ADR-0006 decision 2, written the previous day and merged that morning by this same process. POST /v1/search does carry a truncation signal; the ADR said it did not; and notion-api-practice.md section 4.5 had listed SearchResponse correctly since the day before. The ADR contradicted a file sitting in the repository. Worst moment, and it is that: a negative was asserted across three endpoints having opened two, and silence on a shared pagination page was read as absence rather than as not-checked. The finding underneath survived and got stronger, because SDK PR #711 omits ListBlockChildrenResponse, so the traversal spine's missing signal now rests on two independent sources instead of on the same inference that had just failed.

The session took #21 as a transcription job and found three things the issue had not specified. #21 was well drafted: it named the wrong row, named the two primary sources, and listed four things the superseding ADR must do. The first move was to distrust it anyway and re-fetch both sources -- the post-search reference and notion-sdk-js PR #711 -- because the error being corrected was caused by trusting a page that had not been opened, and inheriting the correction's evidence would have repeated the method while fixing the instance. Both confirmed. One thing the issue did not mention came back with them: the search reference documents no cap constant, so ADR-0006 decision 4's exclusion of search from the cap-proximity trip survives on exactly its stated reason. A signal is not a cap. FINDING 1, and it changes how the error should be read: it was inert. ADR-0006 decision 1 makes the truncation test positive, so the scan looks for request_status on every response page and never consults the table to decide whether to look. A wrong None in a descriptive column gates nothing, and if search never emits the field the behaviour is identical to the old table. The correction has no downside branch. That is containment by a decision made for another reason, not a defence, and the ADR says so -- a negative in a table that DID gate behaviour would have shipped. FINDING 2 contradicts the issue's own framing and is the one worth carrying: the coverage benefit does not reach v0.1. #21 states that the correction makes the ~11,200 wall a reportable gap. True of the endpoint, false of the product, because no document in the repository gives POST /v1/search a role in a scan. Five design surfaces were opened -- ADR-0002 (rejected search as a grant-enumeration instrument), CONTEXT.md (declared roots are operator-named, nothing discovers them), PRODUCT.md (the manifest names only what was declared or enumerated), #18's hydration map (four rules, four fetch depths, no search), and the 2026-08-17 proof run (data-source query and block children only). All five are silent. The ADR states their silence and refuses to assert the negative, because misreading silence as absence is the error it exists to correct; filed as #24 instead of decided. FINDING 3 sharpens the standing method rule. The fact was not in one research file, it was in two, and both predate ADR-0006 by about three hours -- notion-api-practice.md 4.5 and competitive-landscape.md 4, both in 12106c5 at 18:51 against f8917fa at 21:42, ancestry confirmed with git merge-base --is-ancestor. So the grep that would have caught this was not a coin flip against thin evidence. Second ADR to contradict a file already in the tree; the enforcement question is #25 rather than a hook installed unilaterally, because two occurrences justify writing the rule down and a permanent tax on every ADR write wants a third. ADR-0006's central finding came out stronger than it went in. The claim that GET /v1/blocks/{id}/children carries no truncation signal rested on documentation silence when written -- the same inference that failed on the search row -- and now rests on PR #711 enumerating seven response types and omitting ListBlockChildrenResponse. An SDK that names seven and skips the eighth is a statement about the eighth. The pass that broke one row re-evidenced the row that matters. Two smaller things. docs/agents/domain.md used 'ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders)' as a placeholder example and now collides with a real ADR; renumbered to ADR-00NN. And a PreToolUse hook caught the PR body shipping without a Revisit-if -- the ADR had a full one, the PR did not, and the reviewer reads the PR first. Appended rather than argued with.

scope: #20 -- ADR-0008 baseline state machine and exit-code contract
entry: Two of the issue's premises broke under drafting. `suppressed` is not a baseline state: SARIF's baselineState enum is new/unchanged/updated/absent and suppression is a separate object, so merging them makes 'new AND suppressed' inexpressible -- the third enum-mixing-two-axes finding in this project. And keying exit status on the report disposition would have made the baseline permanently inert, because ADR-0005 decision 3's unqualified carries a conformity clause, so one baselined violation downgrades every run forever; the exit contract now reads the sufficiency clause only. Two findings the issue did not contain: resolved became a coverage claim requiring the (rule,resource) pair to have reached evaluated, otherwise the baseline shrinks because access shrank -- a failure ESLint ships today. And the fingerprint kill criterion was NOT cleared: drafting asserted page-ID stability as an obvious UUID property, and ADR-0007's mandatory grep returned notion-api-documented.md section 596 recording it as documented-silent with only a negative search result behind it. That rule paid for itself once, which is the third data point #25 was waiting on. Prior art fetched directly: fsck bitmask, pytest exit 5, rsync 23/24, ESLint and grep exit 2, POSIX 2.8.2. A bitmask was rejected -- it permits states the model forbids and re-allocates the number ADR-0002 spent.

scope: #1 -- ADR-0009 credential model and the Operator definition
entry: Operator was used 35 times across docs/adr/, CONTEXT.md and PRODUCT.md with no definition, including inside other glossary entries. Opening the connection-types page made that untenable: personal access tokens are a second credential model whose denominator is a named employee's access. The operator supplied a verdict (integration primary, PAT secondary with principal attribution) and it was adopted with three amendments. The substantive one: the proposal required any change in the principal's membership to surface as a coverage-boundary change, which is unimplementable -- no endpoint returns a user's accessible set, so neither side of the comparison exists, and ADR-0002 decision 4 was refuted for exactly that shape. Split into detected (principal change) versus disclosed (membership drift under a fixed principal), with a falling coverage ratio explicitly barred as a detector. Also defined Executor and Consumer, added Principal as a new term rather than dual mode-labelled definitions, and recorded the rule that had silently produced three prior decisions: a value is distinct when its remedy is distinct.

commit: d8cebd7 (PR #30, OPEN, closes research half of #27)
entry: The platform launched 2026-05-13 and no file in docs/research/ mentioned it. Six questions, all answered from primary sources, none by observation. The decisive finding rules out the PAT and not by the test the issue planned: a PAT offers exactly two capability options and the API one is a single bundle including create and update, so it violates Principle 7 at the credential layer regardless of which endpoints the code calls. The planned fixture run is therefore no longer decision-relevant. ADR-0002's Revisit-if has NOT fired -- a Worker's access is entirely a function of the token it carries and no enumeration endpoint appeared for any connection type. Workers can be read-only via an integration token but have no exit byte, both output shapes reopen a stated boundary, and they have been billed since 2026-08-11 on credits consumed per run and scaled by run duration -- a meter that charges more the more completely the scan reads, which is adverse in shape rather than in magnitude. One finding landed on ADR-0009, merged the same day: its independence claim was asserted into a documented silence.

commit: (no commit) analytical thread -- issues #29 and #31 filed
entry: The longest phase produced no commit and the most value. Reading notion-user-pain.md in full refuted the session's own zero-config argument: the pain inversion is loudness-versus-testability, not configured-versus-not, and willingness-to-configure is strongest exactly where the testable pains are voiced. The operator's intuition about the MAGNITUDE of user frustration then produced the session's largest finding -- section 4 shows the fury attaches to silent failure rather than to mess, and every high-intensity item across the repository is one defect class: a system reporting success over an unverified state. That reframes the product as an anti-false-green instrument and dissolves the engineer-versus-auditor fork the session had forced an hour earlier. Separately the operator named the real gap as missing CS rigour rather than ticket triage, and was proved right within the hour by the transitivity defect in ADR-0008 decision 6, filed as #31.

Caught during session-start claim verification, not during the work. domain.md said 'four separate incidents' in its intro and 'Three incidents in two distinct shapes' over an enumeration listing three shapes whose first is explicitly two ADRs. Four incidents in three shapes. The S009 close records correcting this exact count in two files; the corrected number reached neither of these two lines. The standing rule that a refuted claim is never in one place fired on the file that states the rule. Grepped for the claim elsewhere: it stands in checkpoint.md line 224, which is a dated band record and correct as a record, so it was left.

#31 reported one defect in ADR-0008 decision 6. Drafting found three more, all inside decision 6 and all one root cause: it loaded whole identity into the fingerprint map. (1) the non-transitive relation as filed; (2) it contradicts ADR-0003 decision 1, the anchor ADR, without citing it -- ADR-0003 chose SARIF's correlationGuid path and decision 6 used the fingerprints path ADR-0003 had examined and rejected; (3) both keys carry the normalized observed value, which is evidence, so a value change breaks both keys at once and ADR-0008's own `updated` state becomes unreachable in exactly the case its remedy column describes; (4) both keys are property-composed, so REF001 and SYS001 are unrepresentable and two broken links on one page get identical maps. The Bannister sweep ran before the instrument was specified and found the problem is deterministic record linkage with a named technique -- hierarchical matchkeys. Wray 2024 (ONS, DOI 10.23889/ijpds.v9i5.2656) supplied the constraint #31's fix lacked: records can only be linked once, matched records leave the pool. #31 had independently reconstructed the field's standard answer and was missing one-to-one. Adopted pass-ordered matching over #31's per-finding probing because a pass is a set join and has no visiting order at all.

Branch chosen as LOGIC rather than UI: the question was whether the state model is right, and that also cleared both gates blocking step 2 -- a single HTML file needs no npm dependency and no token, and the walkthroughs replay recorded proof observations which outrank a fresh call on a question of fact. The red test passed. The larger result is the case it does not cover: reconnect the link target, leave the revoked child revoked, and the scan reports unqualified, exit 0, verdict rendered -- a clean run over a workspace containing a page it cannot see. Not a defect in the model; proof section 4 rendered honestly. The red test passes today only because the REF001 link finding happens to be firing, not because anything detected the revocation. 27 assertions, executed rather than asserted.

First API call any code in this project has made. Eight reads, Notion-Version 2026-03-11, tsc --noEmit clean under strict, @notionhq/client pulls exactly one package with zero advisories. The red test passed on live data via DISCOVERED links. Three defects found in my own implementation, all the product's own defect class: the host allow-list omitted app.notion.com so zero links were discovered with no error; the applicable set was built from child_page only so a child_database was invisible and coverage read 2/2 over a root with three children; and the exit byte read the findings list while the gap lived only in the manifest, returning 1 where the contract requires 3. A fourth, already forbidden: the manifest was keyed on titles and double-counted one resource against CONTEXT.md's settled default. Observed<T> itself never misbehaved on any case -- every defect was in the code around it.

The observed evidence landed on main while the prototype stayed on the throwaway branch, per the prototype skill's capture split. Records REF001 confirmed working end to end, exit 3 outranking exit 1 as ADR-0008 decision 2's priority order observed firing for the first time, and five prior claims re-confirmed first-hand including proof section 4's vanishing child_page. Two rules stated that were written nowhere before: a link recogniser has three outcomes not two, the third being unrecognised; and the applicable set is derived from the enumerated response, never from the subset the scan can classify. Only app.notion.com is evidenced as a link host and the document explicitly declines to claim the other four.

Answers #34's fork -- an unrecognised link is ADR-0005's `undecidable`, not a new axis value -- on four independent lines rather than by assertion: the project's own deletion test (the remedies are identical word for word), the relocation of #34's counter-argument to the manifest cause taxonomy, XCCDF 1.1.4's notchecked/unknown split, and LinkChecker's shipping two-outcome handler where neither outcome is silence. The section 0.5 sweep's decisive hit was the soundiness manifesto, which names this exact false-green in 2015 and prescribes disclosure of the unhandled set rather than a new verdict value. The sweep also killed the spec's assumed shape before drafting: Notion documents custom domains for Sites, so a page can be served from a domain Notion does not own, the host set is unbounded, no allow-list is completable, and #34's own first Revisit-if fires before the spec exists. Consequence adopted -- the residue path is primary and the host list is an optimisation. Only app.notion.com is observed and only *.notion.site is documented; notion.so, www.notion.so and notion.com are marked not checked and kept out of the allow-list with the settling check named. Adds docs/spec/ as a directory at the same evidence class as docs/adr/, differing in scope not authority, and a spec never supersedes an ADR.

34 assertions, offline, no network and no .env; tsc --noEmit clean under strict. Closes #34 DoD item 4. The previous red test could not exercise discovery because discovery was welded to a live client, so link-recognition.ts is the seam that makes the mechanism testable alone. Test 1b is the substantive part: it removes app.notion.com from the host list and asserts the discovery goes red, so the control demonstrates its own sensitivity instead of asserting it -- which requires the host list to be a parameter rather than a module constant. Test 1c executes the regex the first implementation actually shipped and shows the same defect now degrades to a reported gap. Two corrections the spec forced on the prototype: the host list narrowed by four unlocatored entries, and the residue stopped being a hand-pushed finding and entered the manifest so SYS001 derives from one source. verdict.ts exists so the live run and the offline checks execute one implementation of disposition, ratios and exit byte.

The spec's own test suite refuted the spec on its first run. Section 5 claimed an unrecognised reference could exit 0 once coverage sits at or above the declared threshold. It cannot: a coverage gap carries a SYS001 finding and ADR-0008 decision 2 fires exit 1 on any finding that is new and unsuppressed, so raising the threshold lands on exit 1 rather than exit 0. Exit 0 with an unrecognised link therefore requires the operator to have BASELINED the gap -- an explicit recorded decision, not a configuration tweak -- which is the stricter and correct bar. The ADR outranks the spec and the spec was the defect. Recorded because it was found by executing the check rather than by re-reading the reasoning, which is the same route by which the three false-green defects were found on 2026-08-17.

The 0.5 sweep found a formal literature that ten ADRs had never opened, and it changed the answer twice over. A grep of docs/ for coverage-criteria terms returned one line in a raw scout file. Ammann and Offutt give the model -- a coverage criterion imposes test requirements drawn from the criterion's own structure, so the unit varies by criterion by construction -- and XCCDF 1.2 gives the aggregation as a correction it had to make: Appendix B records that scoring moved from per-rule-result to per-Rule because rules with many instances dominated the pooled total. This project was one implementation away from the same defect. Two findings went beyond issue #36's own framing. First, #36's table records REQ001's unit as Resource and that is wrong: a property value can fail independently of its page, so the unit is a (resource, required property) pair -- marked documented, not observed. Second, UNQ001 quantifies over pairs, so reading 90 of 100 resources evaluates 4005 of 4950 pairs, 80.9 percent rather than 90, and at half coverage 24.7 rather than 50. The overstatement runs in the flattering direction, which makes it the product's own false-green defect class arriving inside the coverage machinery built to detect it. ADR-0008 decision 5 had already said the pair, not the resource, is the unit -- for the baseline alone. The ADR generalises a move the repository had made once and not noticed.

Gate 1 closed, and the literature sweep behind #40 turned out to be the smaller half of it. ADR-0005 decision 3's unbounded-gap-cannot-be-sized claim SURVIVES: the field's general result is that no upper bound on an unseen population is available (Alfo/Bohning/Rocchetti 2020 DOI 10.1111/biom.13265; Mao/Huang/Zhang 2016 DOI 10.1111/biom.12553), and every estimator that does produce a bound -- Chao1, ACE, jackknife, Good-Turing, Horvitz-Thompson -- runs on a frequency-of-frequencies distribution needing the same unit observed more than once. Cursor pagination returns each child exactly once, so singletons equal n and doubletons are zero by construction; the input does not exist. The conclusion holds and the ADR's stated reason should be replaced, which is a stronger result than a plain yes. The sweep also created a Revisit-if that did not exist -- two independent enumerations over identifiable IDs WOULD supply that distribution, and the project has two paths (block children, POST /v1/search, #24) -- with the hazard attached: both share one permission grant, positive dependence biases the estimate DOWN, and a downward-biased estimate reports a smaller gap than the true gap. Flattering direction, false-green class, inside the coverage instrument. The larger half needed no literature at all. PRODUCT.md contradicted itself two sections apart: the config-file section concluded declared rules are not the entry point, and the Gates section went on recruiting five teams holding audit-relevant data, which IS that entry point. The product section had absorbed the decay synthesis on 2026-08-16, cited four times; the Gates section never did. WebSearch was dead at 200/200 before the session started, so the sweep ran on a Wiley corpus plus Crossref -- four of eight quotes verified publisher-independently, four marked unverified, ACM and IEEE venues marked not-checked rather than absent.

The /to-spec step this project had never run, and it invented nothing. Issue #10 already held a spec: its Proof checks section is nine falsifiable end-to-end acceptance criteria, written before S005 and never run as a set. The slice seeds from those nine, maps each to the ADR decision governing it -- which is what makes the decides-nothing-new claim checkable rather than asserted -- and scopes to SYS001 and REF001, REF001 because CONTEXT.md names it the load-bearing coverage mechanism after a child_page block vanished from its parent's child list on 2026-08-17. The spec carries a red test before a green one: disable coverage-gap detection and criterion 7 must go red, because a control that passes with its mechanism bypassed tested nothing. docs/agents/domain.md widened docs/spec/ from per-rule to per-rule-and-per-slice rather than adding a directory.

Recorded the five tracer-bullet build tickets: #42 scaffold blocks everything and is blocked by nothing, #43 SYS001 and #44 REF001 run in parallel behind it, #45 reports and the coverage vector behind both, #46 the red test behind that. These are the first tickets on this board that /implement can take. Every previously open issue produced a document, a decision, or a spec -- which is why the board closed 7 and filed 6 across S008-S012 without converging.

Two defects shipped in the merged spec, both already corrected in a triage comment on #10 that this session never read -- the issue BODY was read and its COMMENTS were not. Same shape as the docs/inputs omission the same session had just finished fixing, and it fired twice in one session. THE FINDING: the request budget is bound by block-tree shape, not by workspace size. The estimate is a formula and it reproduces this project's only call log at exactly 7 requests; everything larger is labelled extrapolation from n=1 rather than presented as an estimate. At 150 resources a run costs ~315 requests at 8% block nesting and ~495 at 20%, against 540 derived from 3 req/s and the three-minute kill criterion. The resource count contributes one request each; the recursive descent contributes one per block with children and is unbounded in the shape of the content. A third-party tier-(C) figure agrees from outside: one 250-block page with 50 toggles costs 103 calls, 19% of the budget, on one page. Consequence: PRODUCT.md's warm-scan kill criterion cannot be predicted from a resource count.

title: the negation-as-failure type check
what: A section-0.5 sweep ran BEFORE any instrument was designed - three scouts, three literatures - and refuted this session's own first proposal. Consumer-driven contract testing does not transfer: Pact's FAQ rules out public APIs, bi-directional CDCT swaps provider CI for a provider-published spec we lack, and Spring Cloud Contract tests against a stub built from our own contract. Landed as docs/research/vendor-assumption-drift-prior-art.md with the raw reports and every blocked-route table under sweep-raw/.
finding: The API cannot do X, derived from we looked and found no way, is NEGATION AS FAILURE under a closed-world assumption rather than a negation (DOI 10.1155/2013/632319). Our four reversals are a type error visible on the face of the sentence, detectable with no network call, no corpus and no model. It also explains four-of-four structurally with no appeal to bias: a positive claim is monotonic under vendor change, a negation-as-failure claim is nonmonotonic by construction, and the vendor shipping anything at all is the new information.
decision: slice/negation.ts flags a vendor-negative sentence carrying no type. It is the FIRST check here that flags an UNANNOTATED sentence - CHECK-claims.ts only evaluates claims that were declared, and its header states that hole. Identity is a digest of the sentence, never the line number. Baseline not suppression; a stale entry FAILS. No baseline generator: the one that wrote the initial 22 was deleted in the same commit, because a regenerate command accepts every new negative claim at once.
cost: 22 sentences over 20 decision surfaces, 15 of them in ADRs that may never be edited, so those baseline entries are permanent by design. The vendor claim kind checks FORM only - the gate is offline and that property is worth more than the check - and the mechanical half of a citation control is the only part with no measured error rate.
